- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots — cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at +5% above peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > 0.0) and price is trending upward, model underestimates continuation — add 2–3% to forecast for next 5 days.
- When sentiment swings sharply from negative to positive, model lags — delay upward forecast adjustment by 1–2 days.
- If model forecast mean is consistently above true outcome mean over 3–5 days, apply downward bias correction: subtract 1–2% from next 3-day forecast.
- For sentiment history with high volatility (±0.3+ swings), reduce forecast smoothness — allow ±2% deviation from recent 5-day moving average.
